questions.question: A builder installs an M.2 SSD directly on PCIe lanes and measures 3,500 MB/s reads — far beyond the ~600 MB/s ceiling of SATA/AHCI. Which storage interface protocol is the drive using?
questions.explanation: NVMe is the protocol designed for SSDs on PCIe lanes, bypassing the SATA/AHCI bottleneck.

questions.question: A motherboard spec sheet says the CPU's own lanes serve only RAM and PCIe slots, while USB, SATA, and Ethernet all hang off one companion chip managing data flow to peripherals. Which component is this?
questions.explanation: The chipset (modern PCH) is the motherboard traffic controller linking the CPU to slower I/O devices.

questions.question: Task Manager reports 8 'logical processors' on a 4-core CPU because each physical core interleaves two instruction streams. Which Intel technology creates these logical processors?
questions.explanation: Intel's Hyper-Threading (SMT) presents each physical core as two logical processors — 4 cores become 8 threads.

questions.question: On a 2005-era PC, every CPU request to RAM and the northbridge crosses one shared pathway that bottlenecks faster processors. Name this legacy CPU-to-memory bus.
questions.explanation: The Front Side Bus was the shared CPU-to-northbridge/RAM path before point-to-point links like QPI and DMI.

questions.question: A technician flashes a new BIOS by electrically erasing and rewriting the firmware chip in place — no removal and no UV lamp needed. Which type of ROM chip enables this?
questions.explanation: EEPROM can be erased and rewritten electrically in circuit, which is what firmware updates rely on.

questions.question: When a user picks Sleep, the OS commands the hardware into the low-power S3 state and restores it on wake without touching firmware menus. Which power-management standard defines these OS-controlled states?
questions.explanation: ACPI hands device and system power states (S0–S5) to the operating system.

questions.question: A powered-on PC can't load Windows directly: firmware loads a small boot program, which loads a boot loader, which loads the kernel — pulling the system up 'by its bootstraps.' Name this staged startup process.
questions.explanation: Bootstrapping is the staged chain in which each small loader loads the next, larger stage.

questions.question: A CPU upgrade fails because the new chip's 1700 contact pads will not fit the old board's 1200-pin receptacle, even though both processors are Intel. Which motherboard part must physically match the CPU?
questions.explanation: The socket's pin/pad layout (e.g., LGA1200 vs LGA1700) must exactly match the CPU's package.

questions.question: A CPU datasheet lists 'DDR4-3200 support' because the component that talks directly to RAM now sits inside the processor die instead of a separate northbridge. Name that component.
questions.explanation: Modern CPUs integrate the memory controller on-die, which is why supported RAM speeds are a CPU spec.

questions.question: A gamer raises a CPU's multiplier from 36x to 45x and adds voltage; benchmarks improve but temperatures spike and the warranty is void. What is this tuning practice called?
questions.explanation: Running hardware beyond manufacturer-rated clocks for extra performance is overclocking.

questions.question: A user installs a 250 W GPU on a 400 W PSU and the PC shuts down under load; which PSU spec matters here?
questions.explanation: The PSU's wattage rating must exceed the total power draw of all components or the system shuts down under load.

questions.question: Tracing one instruction, an engineer watches the CPU read it from RAM, interpret its opcode, then perform the operation — a cycle repeated billions of times a second. Name this three-stage cycle.
questions.explanation: Every instruction passes through fetch (read), decode (interpret), and execute (perform).

questions.question: A laptop CPU rated at 2.4 GHz briefly reports 4.2 GHz while exporting a video, then drops back as temperatures climb. Which Intel feature enables these temporary speed bursts?
questions.explanation: Turbo Boost opportunistically raises clocks above base frequency within thermal and power limits.

questions.question: Before a long flight on a dying battery, the user picks the power option that writes the entire session to disk and powers fully off, resuming exactly where it stopped next boot. Which power state is this?
questions.explanation: Hibernation saves the session to disk (unlike sleep, which keeps RAM powered), allowing a complete power-off.

questions.question: After a heatsink was remounted dry, idle CPU temperatures jumped 20 °C; applying a thin layer of compound to fill microscopic air gaps between heat spreader and heatsink fixed it. What material was applied?
questions.explanation: Thermal paste displaces insulating air in microscopic gaps, restoring heat conduction to the heatsink.

questions.question: A CPU is rated at 3.2 GHz. Roughly how many clock cycles does it complete in 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: 3.2 GHz means 3.2 billion cycles per second; multiplied by 5 seconds gives 16 billion cycles.

questions.question: A PC takes 40 seconds to reach the desktop from a hard drive but only 10 seconds after cloning the same data to an SSD. Which storage property, not capacity, explains the difference?
questions.explanation: SSDs have near-zero access times and far faster random reads, so scattered boot files load much quicker than from spinning platters.

questions.question: A user upgrades from 8 GB to 16 GB of RAM and heavy multitasking stops stuttering. Which disk-based memory technique had previously been overused, causing the slowdown?
questions.explanation: When RAM fills, the OS swaps memory pages to disk (paging); the extra RAM reduces this slow disk traffic.

questions.question: A game uses 100% of the CPU but only 40% of the GPU, capping frame rates. What is the common name for this performance imbalance?
questions.explanation: The slowest component limits the whole system; here the CPU bottleneck starves the GPU of work.

questions.question: A desktop boots to a black screen whenever a USB flash drive is left plugged in, but starts Windows normally without it. Which BIOS/UEFI setting should the technician adjust?
questions.explanation: The firmware is attempting to boot from USB first; moving the internal drive above USB in the boot order fixes it.
